items: Ocean Science Bowl: 1,759 more questions from regional bowl teams (Blue Heron Bowl, Lake Sturgeon Bowl) and a 2017 NOSB practice set.
Read aloud: degrees are read as degrees ("25 degrees Celsius", and "naught" for ΔH°), and ion charges as charges ("Fe 3 plus", "CO 3 2 minus") instead of "to the".

Read aloud: when a question says how to read an equation or formula ("[READ: x squared plus y squared …]"), the voice reads that instead of the symbols; reader notes like "[read slowly]" are no longer read out.
Read aloud: words are said as written again, and printed pronunciation guides are skipped, since some voices were spelling the respellings out letter by letter.
Read aloud: shorter pauses between multiple-choice options.

Read aloud: pronunciation guides are reworded so voices don't spell out pieces like "sih" (siliceous) or garble endings (achondroplasia); words on the site's pronunciation list now win over a packet's guide.
Help: this changelog.
Rooms: a player whose device doesn't have the host's voice now has it sped up or slowed down to keep the host's pace.
Read aloud: hard terms are said from the packet's own pronunciation guide, or from a list of about 260 respelled scientific names and terms.
Stats: a toss-up attempts bar (correct, wrong, negs), points per toss-up by subject, and buzz point by subject.
A Search Google button after each question, searching the whole question and its answer choices.
Wrong early buzzes are called negs, as in real Science Bowl.
Answer checking: answers with variables are compared by value (1/4 omega matches ω/4), and LaTeX degree signs are understood.
Stats: recent questions show their set, round and number.
4,529 questions added: MOOSE, NCB 2026, Lexington Biology Bowl 2026, the 2023-24 Roundshare and more. LOST2 removed, since its scanned packet couldn't be read reliably.
Answer checking: numbered statements can be answered by name, the question's noun can be left off (O for "what horizon"), and a different number is never a typo.
Questions search: fixed highlighting on long searches.

Read aloud became listen mode: the question is only heard, and its text shows after. Short pauses before answer choices; in rooms the host picks one voice for everyone; voices no longer stop mid-word.
Ocean Science Bowl: an SB / OSB switch with 801 NOSB questions.
8,841 questions from 18 more tournaments.
Random order spreads questions evenly across the six main subjects.
Room settings are remembered between rooms; a home-screen icon for iPhone.
Questions tab: easier paging, and the round filter lists every round of the picked set.
Rooms: a ping badge; ruling an earlier buzz correct voids later buzzes.
15,888 questions from 33 more tournaments.
Each question starts with its subject and type; Roman-numeral lists accept numbers.
Filter by round stage: round robin, early, mid or late double elimination.
An IsoBowl-style scoreboard.
Saved questions (bookmarks), lenient "all" answers, and math answers compared by value.
13,588 questions from MIT, Stanford, Texas, MOSFET and 20 more tournaments; large banks load fast.
